newsitem.title: JAPAN: Cosmo Oil buys May-lifting Nigeria Bonny Light.
newsitem.headline: Cosmo Oil buys May-lifting Nigeria Bonny Light.

text.p: Cosmo Oil, a leading Japanese refiner, said on Thursday it had purchased a volume comparable to a very large crude carrier (VLCC) of Nigerian Bonny Light crude for May-lifting.
It is the first time Cosmo has bought Nigerian crude since February last year, a company spokesman said.
He said the crude was purchased at a price related to Dated Brent, but declined to be more specific.
The cargo is due to be shipped around May 20, and arrive in Japan a month later, to be processed at Cosmo's refineries in Yokkaichi in central Japan and Sakai in western Japan, the spokesman said.
The decision to purchase Bonny Light crude was made because of a recently narrow Brent/Dubai spread which make West African crude cargoes a financially attractive choice, he said.
The discount of Asian benchmark Dubai crude to North Sea bellwether Dated Brent is the primary trigger for the flow of Brent-linked crudes into Asia.
Japan imported an average of 19,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Nigerian crude in the first quarter of this year and an average of 27,000 bpd in 1996.
Nigeria is Japan's principal source of West African crude.
Other West African suppliers include Gabon, Angola, and Congo.
